faq.question: What is the first block on a local landing page?
faq.answer: Use a direct service + location answer, then immediately support it with proof, reviews or examples.

faq.question: How should local pages interlink?
faq.answer: Link from the main service page to local pages, from local pages back to the core offer, and between related proof resources.

faq.question: What should be avoided?
faq.answer: Avoid generic city-swapped text, fake local claims, hidden content and pages without a real contact or quote path.

cta.title: Turn local landing pages into proof-led conversion paths
cta.body: Check which local pages deserve indexation and which need stronger proof before release.

local-service-seo.seo_title: Local Service SEO for AI Search and Bing Discovery | Base2026
local-service-seo.meta_description: Local service SEO for AI visibility: GBP, reviews, service pages, proof, citations, schema and internal links that support buyer prompts.

answer_capsule.heading: Local service SEO is the source footprint behind the recommendation.
answer_capsule.body: A local service business needs consistent profiles, strong service pages, reviews, proof, schema and internal links so search and AI systems can verify what to recommend.

faq.question: What should a local service business fix first?
faq.answer: Fix service clarity, Google Business Profile data, review proof, location coverage, contact paths and indexability of the main pages.

faq.question: How does this relate to Bing?
faq.answer: Bing needs crawlable canonical URLs, sitemap inclusion, internal links and useful page-level facts for discovery and grounding eligibility.

faq.question: What is the local SEO trap?
faq.answer: Chasing hundreds of weak location pages before fixing core service pages and proof usually creates crawl waste.

cta.title: Prioritize local SEO work that creates leads
cta.body: Use a diagnostic pass to choose the pages and proof signals most likely to influence buyers.

local-seo-gbp.seo_title: Local SEO GBP Signals for AI Visibility | Base2026
local-seo-gbp.meta_description: How Google Business Profile signals connect to local SEO, source trust, reviews, service pages and AI visibility.

answer_capsule.heading: GBP supports local entity trust when it matches the website and reviews.
answer_capsule.body: Categories, services, location, reviews, hours and links should reinforce the same facts shown on service pages and other public profiles.

faq.question: Can GBP alone create AI visibility?
faq.answer: No. It supports local context, but the website, reviews, citations and proof pages need to agree with it.

faq.question: Which GBP signals should be checked?
faq.answer: Check primary category, services, description, hours, locations, reviews, photos, booking/contact links and consistency with the site.

faq.question: How does GBP connect to Bing work?
faq.answer: Even though GBP is a Google surface, the consistency of public local facts also supports broader entity trust and source-footprint checks.

cta.title: Connect GBP to the rest of the visibility system
cta.body: Audit whether local profiles, pages and reviews tell one consistent story.

reviews-local-seo.seo_title: Reviews, Local SEO and AI Visibility | Base2026
reviews-local-seo.meta_description: How reviews support local SEO and AI visibility when they align with service pages, proof, entities and answer-ready content.

answer_capsule.heading: Reviews are proof signals, not just reputation widgets.
answer_capsule.body: Useful reviews reinforce services, locations, outcomes and trust. They become stronger when service pages and profiles reference the same claims accurately.

faq.question: How do reviews help AI visibility?
faq.answer: Reviews can corroborate service quality, locations and recurring customer language that answer engines may use when evaluating trust.

faq.question: Where should review proof appear?
faq.answer: Place relevant review snippets near service, location, proof and conversion sections without fabricating or overclaiming.

faq.question: What review pattern is risky?
faq.answer: Fake reviews, copied testimonials, unsupported star claims and review text hidden from users can damage trust.

cta.title: Use review language as proof, not decoration
cta.body: Find where reviews should support service pages and local proof before adding more generic content.

owned-branded-review-pages.seo_title: Owned Branded Review Pages for AI Visibility | Base2026
owned-branded-review-pages.meta_description: How owned review and proof pages can support branded search, local trust and AI visibility without fake or thin testimonial content.

answer_capsule.heading: Owned review pages should organize real proof around buyer decisions.
answer_capsule.body: The page should explain what customers say, which services the reviews support, where third-party proof lives, and how the buyer can verify the claims.

faq.question: Should a business create a review page?
faq.answer: Yes, if it adds useful context, links to third-party profiles, groups reviews by service or outcome, and avoids fake or duplicated claims.

faq.question: How does it support AI visibility?
faq.answer: It gives crawlers a focused page that connects brand trust, service claims and corroborating review sources.

faq.question: What should it link to?
faq.answer: Link to core service pages, review profiles, case proof, about/entity pages and contact or audit paths.

cta.title: Turn reviews into an evidence page
cta.body: Build proof pages that make real customer trust easier to verify and connect to services.

bottom-of-funnel-seo-landing-pages.target_query: Bottom of funnel SEO landing pages
bottom-of-funnel-seo-landing-pages.seo_title: Bottom-of-Funnel SEO Landing Pages for AI Search | Base2026
bottom-of-funnel-seo-landing-pages.meta_description: Bottom-of-funnel SEO landing pages for Bing/Copilot discovery: exact intent, comparison, proof, FAQ, pricing context and conversion path.

answer_capsule.heading: Bottom-of-funnel pages should answer the buying decision directly.
answer_capsule.body: For commercial AI/search prompts, the page should state the offer, who it fits, proof, process, price or package context where possible, FAQ and the action path.

faq.question: What is a bottom-of-funnel search page?
faq.answer: It targets buyers comparing solutions, pricing, providers, audits, implementation options or urgent service choices.

faq.question: What makes it AI-ready?
faq.answer: Direct answers, clear entity/service facts, proof, schema, internal links and concise sections make it easier to retrieve and trust.

faq.question: Should it be long?
faq.answer: It should be complete, not bloated. Put the answer and proof early, then expand only where it helps the buyer decide.

cta.title: Build pages for buyers who are ready to act
cta.body: Use commercial-intent pages to connect AI visibility work to qualified inquiries, not vanity traffic.

transactional-seo-landing-page-structure.seo_title: Transactional SEO Landing Page Structure for AI Visibility | Base2026
transactional-seo-landing-page-structure.meta_description: A practical transactional landing page structure for search and AI visibility: direct answer, proof, offer, FAQ, schema and CTA.

answer_capsule.heading: Transactional pages need an answer, a reason to trust, and a next step.
answer_capsule.body: The page should align title, H1, intro, proof blocks, FAQs and CTA around one transaction-intent query so buyers and crawlers see the same purpose.

faq.question: What sections should a transactional page include?
faq.answer: Use direct answer, offer fit, benefits, proof, process, FAQ, related links, schema and CTA.

faq.question: How is it different from a blog post?
faq.answer: It is built for a buyer decision and conversion path, not general education alone.

faq.question: What should be measured?
faq.answer: Measure indexability, impressions, assisted leads, form starts, scroll/click signals and whether AI/search answers can retrieve the page.

cta.title: Structure transactional pages around the decision
cta.body: Audit whether commercial pages answer the buyer before asking them to convert.

landing-page-conversion.seo_title: Landing Page Conversion and AI Visibility | Base2026
landing-page-conversion.meta_description: How landing page conversion and AI visibility connect through clear offers, trust proof, page structure, internal links and answer-ready copy.

answer_capsule.heading: AI visibility should lead to a page that can convert the buyer.
answer_capsule.body: Discovery is wasted if the landing page does not explain the offer, proof, fit, process and next step in a format a buyer can trust quickly.

faq.question: What conversion elements matter for AI-search traffic?
faq.answer: The page needs a direct offer, trust proof, friction-free contact path, specific FAQs and internal links to deeper evidence.

faq.question: What hurts conversion from search?
faq.answer: Vague hero copy, missing proof, too many CTAs, no service clarity and disconnected lead forms hurt conversion.

faq.question: How does this help Bing?
faq.answer: A focused, crawlable landing page with clear content and links can be discovered and evaluated more reliably than a vague funnel page.

cta.title: Make discovery pages conversion-ready
cta.body: Connect the traffic page to a clear audit, service or quote path before scaling more URLs.

technical-seo-indexing.seo_title: Technical SEO Indexing for Bing and AI Search | Base2026
technical-seo-indexing.meta_description: Technical SEO indexing checklist for Bing/Copilot: canonical URLs, sitemaps, IndexNow, noindex control, crawl paths and page quality gates.

answer_capsule.heading: Indexing work starts with a clean URL ledger and live gates.
answer_capsule.body: Before submitting URLs, verify 200 status, self-canonical, indexable robots, sitemap inclusion, crawlable internal links, no query-state URLs and enough unique content value.

faq.question: What should be submitted through IndexNow?
faq.answer: Submit added, updated or removed canonical URLs that pass live checks and belong to the verified host.

faq.question: What does IndexNow not guarantee?
faq.answer: It does not guarantee crawl or indexation. It tells search engines that a URL changed and should be considered.

faq.question: What should be excluded from indexation?
faq.answer: Exclude noindex pages, redirects, duplicates, thin drafts, query URLs and pages without useful unique content.

cta.title: Build a controlled indexing pipeline
cta.body: Use a gated ledger so only quality, canonical URLs are pushed to Bing and monitored afterwards.

technical-seo-site-crawling.seo_title: Technical SEO Site Crawling for Bing/Copilot Visibility | Base2026
technical-seo-site-crawling.meta_description: Technical crawling checklist for Bing and AI search: internal links, renderable content, sitemap quality, duplicate control and crawl budget protection.

answer_capsule.heading: Crawl quality decides which pages get discovered and refreshed.
answer_capsule.body: A Bing/Copilot-ready site keeps important URLs reachable through links, avoids crawl waste, exposes content in HTML, keeps sitemaps canonical and updates changed URLs with IndexNow.

faq.question: What should a crawl audit check first?
faq.answer: Check status codes, canonical tags, meta robots, internal links, sitemap membership, duplicate patterns, rendering and broken assets.

faq.question: Why does crawl waste matter?
faq.answer: Low-value duplicate URLs, parameters and thin pages can delay discovery of pages that actually matter for visibility and leads.

faq.question: How often should crawling be rechecked?
faq.answer: Recheck after template changes, new page batches, sitemap updates, deployments and major source/content refreshes.

cta.title: Protect crawl budget before scaling pages
cta.body: Use crawl evidence to decide whether to add pages, reinforce links or fix templates first.
